title: Say: He is Allah, the One.
subtitle: The answer to: tell us your Lord's lineage

row.title: one of many
sub: the top of a family of gods

row.title: singular
sub: no rival, no assistant, no equal

then: Ubayy bin Ka'b reported the idolaters said: {trap}O Muhammad, tell us the lineage of your Lord{/trap}. Allah revealed this surah. Ibn Kathir says Ahad means {idea}the One, the Singular, with no peer, no assistant, no rival{/idea}, a word used in affirmation for no one but Allah.
now: You split your trust between many things: the boss, the doctor, the savings, the right connections. Each feels like a small god on a bad day. {idea}This verse gathers your heart back to One.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said this surah equals a third of the Quran.
old: I trust Allah, plus a few other things that keep me safe.
new: There is One. Everything else I lean on is only a means He controls.
try: Recite this surah three times this evening, as the Prophet ﷺ taught, along with Al-Falaq and An-Nas.

title: Allah, the One everything turns to in need.
subtitle: As-Samad: the perfect, self-sufficient Master
then: Ibn Abbas said As-Samad is {idea}the One all creation depends on for their needs and requests{/idea}. He also said it is the Master {reward}perfect in sovereignty, nobility, forbearance, knowledge and wisdom{/reward}. A companion who loved reciting this surah was told Allah loves him.
now: Rent is due, the car broke down, a child is sick. Your first move is a frantic round of calls. {idea}As-Samad is where every need ends up anyway.{/idea} Start there, then make the calls.
old: I go to Allah when other options have failed.
new: Every need in creation goes to As-Samad. I bring mine to Him first.
try: Next time you need something today, make a short dua before picking up your phone.

title: He has no child, and He was born of no one.
subtitle: Above beginnings and endings
then: A narration explains: {idea}nothing is born except that it will die, and nothing dies except that it leaves inheritance{/idea}, and Allah neither dies nor leaves inheritance. The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}no one is more patient with hurtful words than Allah{/reward}: they ascribe a son to Him, and still He feeds and heals them.
now: Everyone you depend on had a beginning and will have an end: your parents, your mentor, you. {idea}The One you worship has neither.{/idea} Whatever you place in His hands will never be orphaned.
old: Everything I rely on can eventually be lost.
new: People I love are born and pass away. Allah does not. My trust in Him never runs out.
try: Think of someone you depend on who will not always be here. Entrust them to Allah in a dua.

title: There is nothing at all like Him.
subtitle: No equal, no comparison
then: Ibn Kathir says it means {idea}none similar to Him, none equal to Him, nothing at all like Him{/idea}. He owns and created everything, so how could any creature equal Him? A man who asked Allah by these words was said to have {reward}asked by His Greatest Name{/reward}.
now: Your fear feels enormous. The diagnosis, the debt, the person who hates you. In your head it has no equal. {idea}This verse puts it back in its place.{/idea} Only Allah has no equal. Everything else, your problem included, is His creation.
old: This problem is the biggest thing in my life right now.
new: Nothing is comparable to Allah. My biggest problem is still small before Him.
try: Make dua tonight using these words: O Allah, the One, As-Samad, who has no equal.
